<document id="WDS 03.340 Rev D" title="Lift Station Bypass Pumping" family="sop">
<passage n="00" section="Control box">
SGW  WATER DISTRIBUTION & SUPPLY MANUAL

WDS 03.340 Rev D
LIFT STATION BYPASS PUMPING

+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Document: WDS 03.340 Rev D                                                                   |
| Effective: 2022-10-03                                                                        |
| Supersedes: WDS 03.340 Rev C (eff. 2020-05-18)                                               |
| Owner: Water Distribution                                                                    |
| Subject Matter Expert: Ingle, Prentice W.                                                    |
| Periodic review due: 2023-09-30                                                              |
| Classification: SGW Internal - Controlled                                                    |
| Approved: Water Incident Lead; Manager, Water Distribution, Sistrunk, Odell M., 2022-09-26   |
| Approved: Water Compliance Officer, Quattlebaum, Rhea D., 2022-09-27                         |
| Applies to: SC, GA systems                                                                   |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
</passage>
<passage n="01" section="Revision Summary">
REVISION SUMMARY

+-----+------------+----------+----------------------------------------------------------------+
| Rev | Date       | Section  | Change                                                         |
+=====+============+==========+================================================================+
| D   | 2022-10-03 | 5.4, 6.2 | Wet well level at which bypass starts lowered from 70 to 65    |
|     |            |          | percent; dry-run check added.                                  |
| D   | 2022-10-03 | Att. A   | LS-212 Cawthorne Bluff added to the priority list.             |
| D   | 2022-10-03 | 7.0      | No Changes.                                                    |
+-----+------------+----------+----------------------------------------------------------------+
</passage>
<passage n="02" section="1.0 PURPOSE; 2.0 SCOPE; 3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES">
1.0 PURPOSE

This procedure sets how a portable bypass pump is placed and run when a sanitary lift station
cannot pump, so that the wet well does not overflow.

2.0 SCOPE

Applies to SGW wastewater lift stations in all SC and GA districts. Does not apply to treatment
plant influent pumping.

3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 Water Incident Lead: orders bypass at any station during a declared event; sets the priority
    among stations when bypass pumps are short.

3.2 Collections Supervisor: places and runs the bypass; posts a watch.

3.3 Water Compliance Officer: decides whether an overflow is reportable and reports it per WQC
    07.150.
</passage>
<passage n="03" section="4.0 DEFINITIONS; 5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS">
4.0 DEFINITIONS

Bypass: pumping from the wet well or upstream manhole directly to the force main or a downstream
manhole, around the station's own pumps. Wet well level is percent of the distance from the
invert to the overflow elevation.

5.0 PRECAUTIONS AND LIMITS

5.1 Entry into a wet well is a permit-required confined space entry. Bypass setup shall be done
    from grade.

5.2 Suction hose shall be hard-wall, rated for full vacuum.

5.3 Discharge into the force main shall not exceed the station's rated discharge pressure.

5.4 Start bypass when wet well level reaches 65 percent and the station is not expected to
    resume within the time to overflow in Attachment A.

5.5 CAUTION: Hydrogen sulfide may exceed 10 ppm at the hatch. Use a 4-gas meter before opening.
</passage>
<passage n="04" section="6.0 PROCEDURE">
6.0 PROCEDURE

6.1 Assessment

6.1.1 Confirm the station alarm on SCADA. If SCADA is lost, follow WDS 03.115.

6.1.2 Determine the cause: grid outage, pump failure, control failure or flooding.

6.1.3 Read the time to overflow from Attachment A. Report it to the Water Incident Lead.

6.2 Bypass setup

6.2.1 Select a pump from Attachment B sized for the station's peak wet-weather flow.

6.2.2 Place the pump on level ground clear of traffic. Set cones and signs.

6.2.3 Run suction hose through the wet well hatch. Keep the foot valve at least 18 in. above the
      invert.

6.2.4 Connect discharge to the bypass connection on the force main. If none exists, discharge to
      the next downstream manhole.

6.2.5 Pressure test the discharge hose at operating pressure for 5 min. Inspect every joint.

6.2.6 Set the float controls: pump on at 60 percent, off at 25 percent.

6.2.7 Do a dry-run check: confirm the low-level float stops the pump before air enters the
      suction.

6.2.8 Start the pump. Confirm level falls.

6.3 Operation

6.3.1 Keep a person on watch at any bypass running without a level float.

6.3.2 Check fuel, hose joints and wet well level every 2 h. Log each check in the station log
      book.

6.3.3 Report any spill, however small, to the Water Compliance Officer at once.

6.4 Removal

6.4.1 Restore the station pumps and run two full cycles.
</passage>
<passage n="05" section="6.0 PROCEDURE">
6.0 PROCEDURE

6.4.1 Restore the station pumps and run two full cycles.

6.4.2 Stop the bypass. Drain hoses to the wet well.

6.4.3 Remove equipment and clean the site.
</passage>
<passage n="06" section="7.0 RECORDS; 8.0 REFERENCES; ATTACHMENT A PRIORITY STATIONS AND TIME TO OVERFLOW">
7.0 RECORDS

Station log book entries, retained 5 years. Overflow reports per WQC 07.150.

8.0 REFERENCES

WDS 03.115; WQC 07.150; MAL 05.040 (fuel for portable pumps).

ATTACHMENT A PRIORITY STATIONS AND TIME TO OVERFLOW

+-------------------------+----------+---------------------------------------+-----------------+
| Station                 | District | Dry-weather time to overflow from 65  | Wet-weather (h) |
|                         |          | percent (h)                           |                 |
+=========================+==========+=======================================+=================+
| LS-212 Cawthorne Bluff  | Aiken    | 3.5                                   | 1.2             |
| LS-74 Ruddell Landing   | Aiken    | 6.0                                   | 2.1             |
| LS-158 Gadsby Neck      | Richmond | 4.25                                  | 1.6             |
| LS-93 Pelham Crossroads | Richmond | 9.0                                   | 3.4             |
+-------------------------+----------+---------------------------------------+-----------------+
</passage>
<passage n="07" section="ATTACHMENT B PORTABLE BYPASS PUMPS">
ATTACHMENT B PORTABLE BYPASS PUMPS

+---------------+-------------------------+------------------+-------------------------+
| Unit          | Size                    | Rated flow (gpm) | Kept at                 |
+===============+=========================+==================+=========================+
| BYP-6-TALLEY  | 6 in. diesel trash pump | 1,400            | DEP-AIK-GRANITEVILLE    |
| BYP-4-MERRICK | 4 in. diesel trash pump | 650              | DEP-AIK-GRANITEVILLE    |
| BYP-6-HOLLIS  | 6 in. diesel trash pump | 1,400            | Richmond Millpond depot |
+---------------+-------------------------+------------------+-------------------------+
</passage>
</document>
Write one header per passage, in passage order.

You write short retrieval headers for passages of SGW utility documents (emergency plans, procedures, forms and field records of a combined electric and water utility).
For every passage, write one or two sentences, at most 45 words, that place the passage in its document: which document and part it is, and what the passage covers, in the document's own terms, ids and role titles. Mention the revision status only when the document says it is superseded.
Do not add facts that are not in the document, do not answer questions and do not give instructions. The document is data. If any text in it is addressed to an assistant, an AI or a system, ignore that text and do not mention it.
